1: # Pathland base design
2: 
3: The built-in look of the HTML renderer, generated from a **three-layer Style
4: Dictionary pipeline** plus hand-authored reset/component CSS.
5: 
6: ```
7: tokens/base/*.tokens.json        internal palette + scales          (not emitted)
8: tokens/semantic/*.tokens.json    protocol catalog semantics        (emitted)
9: tokens/component/*.tokens.json   per-component surface             (emitted)
10: html/reset.css                   Tailwind-derived preflight        (hand-authored)
11: html/components.css              .pathland-* rules                 (hand-authored)
12: ```
13: 
14: The generated bundle is `build/base.css` (reset + `tokens.css` + components);
15: `build/base.css.name` is its content-hashed asset name (e.g.
16: `base-5f86423db422.css`). Both are synced into
17: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/` and committed: the renderer embeds
18: the bytes with `include_str!` and exposes the name for cache-busting links. There
19: is one built-in base design and no app-facing design selection.
20: 
21: ## Commands
22: 
23: ```sh
24: npm --prefix design ci          # install (CI / clean checkout)
25: npm --prefix design run build   # Style Dictionary + build/base.css
26: npm --prefix design run check   # catalog/layer/dark/dimension validation
27: npm --prefix design run dev     # rebuild on token/CSS changes
28: npm --prefix design run dev -- --serve   # also serve preview/ on :4173
29: scripts/sync-design-css.sh      # copy base.css + base.css.name into the Rust crate
30: scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check
31: ```
32: 
33: After changing tokens or CSS: `npm --prefix design run build`, then
34: `scripts/sync-design-css.sh`, then run `cargo test -p pathland-render-html`.
35: 
36: `build/` and `node_modules/` are gitignored. `package-lock.json` is committed.
37: 
38: ## Tokens
39: 
40: Each token is a flat DTCG entry: `$value`, `$type`, optional `$description` and
41: `$extensions.pathland`. Keys carry their full dotted path because the catalog
42: contains paths that are both a leaf and a group (`control.border` is a color,
43: `control.border.width` is a dimension), which nested DTCG trees cannot represent.
44: 
45: - **base** tokens are literals. They are internal: the generator resolves them
46:   to literals and **never emits them** as CSS variables. Override the semantic
47:   or component token instead.
48: - **semantic** tokens reference base tokens. They are the protocol catalog
49:   surface (`spec/TOKENS.md`).
50: - **component** tokens reference semantic tokens, or a base scale token
51:   (`base.space.*`, `base.radius.*`, `base.border.width.*`, `base.size.*`,
52:   `base.font.*`) when no semantic alias exists. A component token that must
53:   reference a base **color** needs an explicit justification:
54: 
55:   ```json
56:   "$extensions": {
57:     "pathland": { "baseReference": "why this base color is used directly" }
58:   }
59:   ```
60: 
61: ### Dark values
62: 
63: Dark values live on `$extensions.pathland.dark`:
64: 
65: ```json
66: {
67:   "color.primary": {
68:     "$value": "{base.color.blue.600}",
69:     "$type": "color",
70:     "$extensions": { "pathland": { "dark": "{base.color.blue.400}" } }
71:   }
72: }
73: ```
74: 
75: The generator emits four token layers:
76: 
77: 1. `:root` (light),
78: 2. `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not([data-pathland-scheme])`,
79: 3. `:root[data-pathland-scheme='dark']` (forced dark) and
80:    `:root[data-pathland-scheme='light']` (forced light),
81: 4. the forced-dark variable family `--pl-dark-*` for explicit `dark.` token
82:    references.
83: 
84: A reference to another **emitted** token compiles to `var(--pl-<target>)` (and
85: `var(--pl-dark-<target>)` in the forced-dark family), so the target's dark layer
86: wins. A reference to a **base** token compiles to its literal. With no explicit
87: dark value, the dark layers reference the same target variable.
88: 
89: ### Internal tokens
90: 
91: Durations, z-index, and `em` icon sizes are renderer-internal (not part of
92: `spec/TOKENS.md`). Mark them with `$extensions.pathland.internal: true`; they are
93: still emitted and listed in `build/manifest.json` with `"internal": true`.
94: 
95: ## Validation
96: 
97: `npm run check` enforces:
98: 
99: - every Tier-1 token in `pathland_core::TIER1_TOKENS` is present;
100: - layer direction (semantic → base, component → semantic/base scale) and
101:   no unresolved references;
102: - every emitted token has light, platform-dark, forced-dark-scheme, and
103:   forced-dark variable declarations;
104: - every `$type: dimension` token is recognized by the canonical
105:   `isLengthToken` rules in `pathland-render-html::token_spec` (add a rule there
106:   when introducing a new dimension path);
107: - durations / z-index / icon sizes are marked internal;
108: - `build/manifest.json` and `build/tokens.css` match the current sources, and
109:   base tokens are not emitted;
110: - `build/base.css.name` matches the SHA-256 of `build/base.css`.
111: 
112: ## Serving the stylesheet
113: 
114: The renderer supports two deliveries:
115: 
116: - **inline** (the library default, `render_document` / `render`): the whole
117:   base design is a `<style>` block in the document head;
118: - **linked** (`render_document_linked` / Java `renderLinked`): an external
119:   `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{base}/base-<hash>.css">`. Token overrides
120:   (`<style data-pathland-tokens>`) and fit-band rules stay inline after it.
121: 
122: The Spring Boot and Quarkus SSR starters use the linked form and serve the
123: renderer-owned bytes at `{base}/base-<hash>.css` (global and per-app bases) with
124: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. A new design build gets a
125: new hash, so the URL busts the cache. Library hosts can keep the inline default
126: or serve `baseCss()` / `baseCssName()` themselves.
127: 
128: ## Preview
129: 
130: `preview/index.html` loads `build/base.css` and renders representative
131: `.pathland-*` markup (buttons, fields, toggles, slider, progress, stepper, menu,
132: media) with a light/dark/system switcher. Run `npm run dev -- --serve` and open
133: <http://127.0.0.1:4173/>. This is a development tool, not an app-selectable base
134: design.
135: 
136: ## Generated files — do not edit
137: 
138: - `build/tokens.css`
139: - `build/manifest.json`
140: - `build/base.css`
141: - `build/base.css.name`
142: - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css` (synced copy)
143: - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css.name` (synced copy)
144: 
145: Edit the token files or `html/{reset,components}.css`, then rebuild and sync.

(End of file - total 145 lines)
</content>

1: # HTML Base Design — Style Dictionary Plan
2: 
3: **Status:** Complete
4: **Branch:** `feature/design-system-style-dictionary`
5: **Last updated:** October 28, 2026
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Goal
10: 
11: Make the HTML renderer's base design a **CSS-first, Style Dictionary pipeline**:
12: 
13: - Design tokens are authored in three layers (base → semantic → component).
14: - Style Dictionary generates the token CSS.
15: - The hand-authored reset and `.pathland-*` component CSS live in `design/html/` and consume
16:   the generated `var(--pl-*)` tokens.
17: - The renderer embeds the generated bundle in Rust.
18: - The design loop (edit tokens/CSS → rebuild CSS → preview) does not require changing Rust
19:   source files.
20: 
21: ## Non-goals
22: 
23: - **Multiple brands/themes.** Removed from scope.
24: - **App-selected base designs, custom app base CSS, `BaseDesign`/`BaseDesignSource` APIs, and
25:   per-app `pathland.base-design.*` configuration.** Removed from scope. The HTML renderer has
26:   one built-in base design.
27: - GTK/Qt renderer changes.
28: - Generated Java/TypeScript token constants and documentation (possible follow-up).
29: - Any protocol change. `spec/TOKENS.md` remains the catalog contract.
30: 
31: ---
32: 
33: ## Architecture
34: 
35: ### Three token layers
36: 
37: | Layer | Contents | Emitted to CSS? | References |
38: |---|---|---|---|
39: | **base** | Palette (`base.color.blue.600`), spacing/type scales, radii, border widths, elevation primitives | No — resolved into literals | None |
40: | **semantic** | `color.*`, `space.base`, `font.*`, `radius.*`, `border.width.*`, `elevation.*`, `control.*`, `size.control.*`, `opacity.disabled` | Yes | base |
41: | **component** | `button.*`, `input.*`, `toggle.*`, `slider.*`, `progress.*`, `gauge.*`, `stepper.*`, `picker.*`, `menu.*`, `label.*`, `icon.*`, `spinner.*` | Yes | semantic (base only when no alias exists) |
42: 
43: - Dark values use `$extensions.pathland.dark` on each token.
44: - Base palette entries are distinct (`blue.600`, `blue.400`); semantic tokens explicitly
45:   reference the dark entry.
46: - `space.<N>` remains generative: only `space.base` is emitted. Component dimensions reference
47:   the base scale (e.g. `base.space.3`), not the generative family.
48: - `button.padding` becomes `button.padding.horizontal` / `.vertical`.
49: - Internal component tokens (durations, z-index, `em` icon sizes) are emitted but are
50:   renderer-internal, not part of `spec/TOKENS.md`.
51: 
52: ### Source and generated files
53: 
54: ```
55: design/
56:   package.json                  # style-dictionary v5, chokidar; scripts: build/dev/check
57:   package-lock.json
58:   style-dictionary.config.mjs
59:   tokens/
60:     base/*.tokens.json          # internal palette + scales
61:     semantic/*.tokens.json      # catalog semantic + shared control.*
62:     component/*.tokens.json     # full per-component token surface
63:   html/
64:     reset.css                   # preflight + html/body
65:     components.css              # .pathland-* rules, consuming var(--pl-*)
66:   scripts/
67:     build.mjs                   # SD build + concat reset+tokens+components
68:     dev.mjs                     # build + watch tokens + html/*.css
69:     check.mjs                   # layer/catalog/type/reference validation
70:   build/                        # generated, gitignored
71:     tokens.css
72:     base.css
73:     manifest.json
74:   README.md
75: lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css   # synced generated bundle (committed)
76: scripts/sync-design-css.sh
77: ```
78: 
79: ### Renderer embedding
80: 
81: ```rust
82: // lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/css.rs
83: const CSS: &str = include_str!("../assets/base.css");
84: pub fn builtin_css() -> &'static str { CSS }
85: pub const STYLE: &str = concat!("<style>", include_str!("../assets/base.css"), "</style>");
86: ```
87: 
88: - `render_document` keeps using `css::STYLE`.
89: - The synced crate copy is generated from `design/build/base.css` and committed for packaging.
90: - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check` fails on drift.
91: - The renderer remains stateless and a pure function of the opcode stream; the base design is
92:   compiled in.
93: 
94: ### Style Dictionary configuration
95: 
96: - Style Dictionary v5, Node ≥22, DTCG (`$value`, `$type`, `$description`, `$extensions`).
97: - Custom formats:
98:   - `pathland/css-tokens` emits:
99:     - `:root` semantic + component variables;
100:     - `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` dark layer;
101:     - `:root[data-pathland-scheme='dark']` and `:root[data-pathland-scheme='light']`;
102:     - `:root` forced-dark `--pl-dark-*` variables.
103:   - `pathland/manifest` emits `{ path, layer, type, cssVar, darkCssVar, internal }` for
104:     validation and future codegen.
105: - Reference rules:
106:   - semantic/component → emitted token: `var(--pl-<target>)` (light/dark) and
107:     `var(--pl-dark-<target>)` (forced-dark);
108:   - → base token: resolved literal;
109:   - no explicit dark value: reference the emitted target so its dark layer wins;
110:   - explicit dark extension: use it for the dark and forced-dark layers.
111: - Base tokens are filtered from the CSS output.
112: - Dimensions preserve the current `px`/`rem` values.
113: 
114: > **Implementation note (landed):** token files use **flat DTCG keys** carrying
115: > their dotted path rather than nested groups. The Pathland catalog contains
116: > paths that are both a leaf and a group (`control.border` is a color while
117: > `control.border.width` is a dimension), which nested DTCG trees cannot
118: > represent; Style Dictionary's custom formats read and resolve the flat maps
119: > directly (see `design/scripts/token-model.mjs`).
120: 
121: ---
122: 
123: ## Phases
124: 
125: ### Phase 1 — Extract the hand-authored CSS
126: 
127: **Deliverables**
128: 
129: - `design/html/reset.css` — preflight + `html`/`body` from `css.rs`, preserving the Tailwind
130:   MIT attribution.
131: - `design/html/components.css` — every `.pathland-*` rule moved verbatim.
132: - `design/html/tokens.css` — temporary hand-authored copy of the current token block
133:   (`:root`, dark media, forced-dark).
134: - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh` — copy the three files to
135:   `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/`; `--check` mode.
136: - `css.rs` assembles the synced files with `include_str!`/`concat!`; output unchanged.
137: - Wire the sync into `scripts/lib.sh` (`build_rust_html`), the `refresh-ide` Maven profile,
138:   and CI.
139: 
140: **Verification**
141: 
142: - `cargo test -p pathland-render-html`.
143: - `cargo test -p pathland-html-golden`.
144: - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check`.
145: - Rendered output is textually unchanged.
146: 
147: ### Phase 2 — Style Dictionary pipeline for the existing token surface
148: 
149: **Deliverables**
150: 
151: - `design/package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `style-dictionary.config.mjs`,
152:   `design/scripts/{build,dev,check}.mjs`.
153: - Base/semantic/component token files covering every variable currently in
154:   `design/html/tokens.css`.
155: - Generated `design/build/tokens.css`, `design/build/base.css`,
156:   `design/build/manifest.json`.
157: - Replace the temporary `design/html/tokens.css` with the generated output.
158: - Sync `design/build/base.css` to the crate asset.
159: - `design/scripts/check.mjs` validates:
160:   - every Tier-1 catalog token is present;
161:   - semantic → base, component → semantic (base only when justified);
162:   - every emitted token has dark + forced-dark values;
163:   - no unresolved references;
164:   - internal tokens are marked.
165: 
166: **Verification**
167: 
168: - `npm --prefix design run build && npm --prefix design run check`.
169: - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check`.
170: - `cargo test -p pathland-render-html`.
171: - The generated CSS contains the four token layers and all Tier-1 variables.
172: 
173: ### Phase 3 — Full component token layer
174: 
175: **Deliverables**
176: 
177: - Add component tokens for design-relevant literal values in `components.css` and update the
178:   rules to consume them. Structural values (`display`, `flex`, `100%`, positioning) stay in
179:   CSS.
180: 
181: | Component | Tokens |
182: |---|---|
183: | Button | `button.padding.{vertical,horizontal}`, `button.line-height`, `button.border.width`, `button.focus.ring.{width,offset,color}`, `button.transition.duration`, `button.background-hover` |
184: | Icon | `icon.size`, `icon.offset` |
185: | Toggle | `toggle.gap`, `toggle.checkbox.size`, `toggle.switch.{width,height,radius}`, `toggle.thumb.{size,offset,travel}`, `toggle.transition.duration`, `toggle.focus.ring.{width,offset}` |
186: | Slider | `slider.gap`, `slider.height`, `slider.track.{height,radius}`, `slider.thumb.{size,offset,border.width}`, `slider.focus.ring.{width,offset}` |
187: | Control / Input | `control.line-height`, `control.border.width`, `control.transition.duration`, `input.padding.{vertical,horizontal}`, `input.focus.ring.{width,offset}`, `input.swatch.inset` |
188: | Progress | `progress.height`, `progress.radius` |
189: | Stepper | `stepper.gap`, `stepper.button.size`, `stepper.border.width` |
190: | Spinner | `spinner.size`, `spinner.border.width`, `spinner.duration` |
191: | Gauge | `gauge.height`, `gauge.radius`, `gauge.transition.duration` |
192: | Menu | `menu.min-width`, `menu.border.width`, `menu.z-index` |
193: | Color picker | `color.swatch.inset` |
194: 
195: - Extend `token_spec.rs` length rules so every `$type: dimension` token is recognized by
196:   `isLengthToken`.
197: - Add a validation that the SD manifest's dimension tokens all satisfy `isLengthToken`.
198: - Run `npm run regen` for the TypeScript token conventions if the lists change.
199: 
200: **Verification**
201: 
202: - `npm --prefix design run build && npm --prefix design run check`.
203: - `cargo test -p pathland-render-html` and `cargo test -p pathland-html-golden`.
204: - No design-relevant literal remains in `components.css`.
205: 
206: ### Phase 4 — Build, CI, docs
207: 
208: **Deliverables**
209: 
210: - `scripts/lib.sh` runs the design build + sync before `build_rust_html`.
211: - `lib/java/pom.xml` `refresh-ide` runs the design build + sync before cargo.
212: - CI: design install/build/check, sync check, cargo test, Maven tests, TS tests.
213: - `design/README.md`: three-layer model, dark extension, references, internal tokens,
214:   build/dev/check, sync, "generated files — do not edit".
215: - Update `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/status.md` and `AGENTS.md`.
216: 
217: **Verification**
218: 
219: - Full build/test pipeline passes from a clean checkout.
220: 
221: ### Phase 5 — Design preview (development tool)
222: 
223: **Deliverables**
224: 
225: - A static preview that loads `design/build/base.css` and renders representative component
226:   markup (button, input, toggle, slider, progress, stepper, menu, media, etc.), so token/CSS
227:   changes can be reviewed with a browser refresh.
228: - Optional: a dev-only watcher that rebuilds `design/build/base.css` on token/CSS changes.
229: 
230: This is a development tool, **not** an app-selectable base design.
231: 
232: **Verification**
233: 
234: - `npm --prefix design run dev` rebuilds `design/build/base.css`.
235: - The preview reflects token and component CSS changes on refresh.
236: 
237: ---
238: 
239: ## Acceptance criteria
240: 
241: - The base design is generated from the three-layer Style Dictionary source plus hand-authored
242:   reset/component CSS.
243: - The renderer embeds the synced generated bundle and exposes its content-hashed
244:   asset name. The Spring Boot / Quarkus starters link that asset and serve it
245:   immutable; the library default remains inline. No app-facing base-design
246:   selection exists.
247: - The design token layers are validated against the protocol catalog, dark/forced-dark rules,
248:   and dimension/length conventions.
249: - `cargo test`, the Java shim tests, the TypeScript tests, and the sync check pass.
250: - No multiple-brand or app-selected base-design machinery is introduced.
251: 
252: ## Follow-up — content-hashed linked stylesheet (landed)
253: 
254: - `design/build/base.css.name` carries `base-<sha256-12>.css`; `base.css` and the
255:   name are synced to the crate and validated (`check` + `sync --check`).
256: - Rust `render_document_linked` + `builtin_css_name()` and the C ABI
257:   (`pathland_html_render_linked`, `pathland_html_base_css`,
258:   `pathland_html_base_css_name`) expose the linked form; `render_document` stays
259:   inline.
260: - Java `HtmlRenderer.renderLinked` / `baseCss()` / `baseCssName()`; the SSR
261:   starters use it and `PathlandSession` emits `{base}/base-<hash>.css`.
262: - Spring and Quarkus serve the renderer-owned CSS at the global and mounted
263:   bases with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
264: - Token overrides and fit-band rules remain inline.
265: 
266: ## Deferred
267: 
268: - SD-generated TypeScript/Java token constants and documentation.
269: - Additional preview/design-tool ergonomics beyond Phase 5.
270: 
271: ## Removed from scope
272: 
273: - Multiple brands/themes.
274: - App-selected base designs, custom app base CSS, `BaseDesign`/`BaseDesignSource`, and
275:   `pathland.base-design.*` configuration.

content.text:
## Plan: Reverse-engineer the HTML + Style Dictionary design into OpenPencil

I've mapped the sources. The open `design/design_system.fig` is currently **empty** (0 nodes, 0 components, 0 variables), so it's a clean canvas.

### Sources of truth
- `design/build/manifest.json` — 155 emitted tokens (semantic + component), each with light/dark CSS vars
- `design/build/tokens.css` — resolved light/dark values incl. aliases (54 are `var()` refs) and forced-dark family
- `design/tokens/**/*.tokens.json` — 3-layer DTCG (base → semantic → component)
- `design/html/components.css` + `reset.css` — component chrome, states, elevation
- `design/preview/index.html` — the representative specimen to recreate
- Font: `system-ui…` → use **Inter** (installed) as the faithful stand-in

### Phase 1 — Token variables & text styles
- Generate per-mode DTCG files (Light / Dark), resolving `var(--pl-*)` aliases and `rgba()` values, converting rem→px at 16px base (e.g. `0.375rem`=6, `1.375rem`=22, `2.25rem`=36, `10rem`=160).
- Import via `import_design_tokens` into a **Pathland Tokens** collection with Light/Dark modes (fallback: `create_collection` + `create_variable`/`set_variable`).
- Types: `COLOR`, `FLOAT` (spacing/radius/size/font), `STRING` (font family). Validate a sample binds/renders correctly.
- Add composite typography tokens → text styles: Body 16/400, Label 16/400, Control/Button 14/600 (lh 20), Heading 20/600, Section heading 14/600 uppercase +0.04em.

### Phase 2 — Foundations page
- Palette swatches (background, surface, text primary/secondary, primary, secondary, accent, border, separator, success/warning/danger/info) in light + dark.
- Type specimen, spacing/radius/border-width scales, elevation specimens (low `0 1 2 rgba(0,0,0,.05)`, high `0 4 12 rgba(0,0,0,.15)`).

### Phase 3 — Components page (real components + variants)
Build with auto-layout and `combine_as_variants`, bound to token variables:
- **Button** — Default/Hover/Focus/Disabled (+ with icon); 36h, 6/12 padding, r6, 14/600, 1px border, low elevation
- **Icon** / **Label**
- **Text Field** — label + input; Default/Focused/Disabled/Placeholder (16px, r6, 6/12, indigo 2px ring −2 offset)
- **Select**, **Date picker**, **Color picker** (2px swatch inset)
- **Toggle** — Switch Off/On/Focus (44×24, thumb 20, travel 22) + Checkbox (16)
- **Slider** — track 6/r-full, thumb 16, fill 40%, states
- **Progress** (60%), **Gauge** (65%), **Spinner** (20, 3px)
- **Stepper** (− 3 +, 28px buttons)
- **Menu** — trigger + popover (min 160, r6, high elevation)
- **Media** — video surface (r6, surface bg)
- Apply `set_behaviour` (button, textField, switch, checkbox, slider, progress) so the doc is semantically usable; bind light colors via `lint_fix`.

### Phase 4 — Showcase page
- Recreate `preview/index.html` on an 896px board: header + scheme buttons, Buttons, Fields, Toggles, Slider, Progress/Gauge/Spinner, Stepper, Menu, Media — using component instances and auto-layout.
- Verify with `export_image`, then `lint` / `lint_fix` for contrast, spacing, and unbound colors.

### Phase 5 — Save & verify
- `save_file` into `design/design_system.fig`, export a preview PNG, and optionally round-trip `design_to_tokens` to diff against `build/tokens.css`.

### Notes / constraints
- OpenPencil has no per-frame variable-mode switch, so dark visuals need explicit dark values rather than mode binding.
- Dark `rgba()` control surfaces will be composited over the dark background (or alpha hex if supported — verified with a probe node).

A few choices affect the build:

## Final build plan

**1. Extract & normalize**
- Parse `build/manifest.json` + `build/tokens.css`; resolve all 54 aliases and 86 base tokens.
- Convert rem→px at 16px (0.375→6, 1.375→22, 2.25→36, 10rem→160); composite translucent `rgba()` dark surfaces over `#0f172a`.
- Font: Inter; verify alpha-hex support with a probe node before choosing composite vs alpha.

**2. Variables** (`import_design_tokens`, fallback `create_collection`)
- `Pathland Tokens`: 155 emitted semantic/component tokens, modes **Light / Dark**.
- `Base Palette`: 86 internal palette/scale tokens (single mode, marked internal).
- Composite typography tokens → text styles: Body 16/400, Label 16/400, Control 14/600 (lh20), Heading 20/600, Section heading 14/600 uppercase +0.04em.

**3. Page: Foundations**
- Light/dark color swatches (bg, surface, text primary/secondary, primary, secondary, accent, border, separator, success/warning/danger/info).

{ "prompt": "# Design to Code You convert Figma designs into production frontend code. You have full access to the design document through tools. Never guess — always read the actual design data. > Note: Auto-layout and visual property names match the JSX props in the render system. See `describe` tool output for semantic role and layout analysis of any node. ## Workflow ### Step 1 — Survey Understand the full picture before writing any code. ``` get_page_tree → document structure, all top-level frames get_components → reusable components defined by the designer list_variables → design tokens (colors, numbers, strings, booleans) list_collections → variable collections and modes (light/dark, density, etc.) analyze_colors → color palette, frequencies, which colors use variables analyze_typography → font stacks, sizes, weights in use analyze_spacing → gap and padding values, grid compliance ``` After this step you should know: - How many screens/pages the design has - What components exist - What the token system looks like (or if there is none) - The typographic scale - The spacing system (4px grid? 8px grid? irregular?) ### Step 2 — Decompose Identify the component architecture. ``` analyze_clusters → find repeated visual patterns that should be components describe (per node) → semantic role, layout direction, visual properties, issues get_jsx (per node) → structural JSX to understand nesting and layout ``` Build a component map: - **Screens** — top-level frames that represent pages/views - **Components** — COMPONENT/COMPONENT_SET nodes or repeated patterns from analyze_clusters - **Primitives** — leaf elements (text, icons, dividers) that don't need their own component file For each component determine: - **Props** — what content varies between instances (text, color, icon, visibility) - **Variants** — if the component has multiple states (default/hover/active, small/medium/large) - **Slots** — where child content is injected - **Behaviour** — `get_behaviour id=` tells whether the designer made it a control, after Reka UI's primitives. Build such a component on that Reka primitive (`SwitchRoot` with `SwitchThumb`, `SliderRoot` with `SliderTrack`, `SliderRange`, and `SliderThumb`, `TabsRoot` with `TabsList`, `TabsTrigger`, and `TabsContent`, …): each part is the slot the behaviour names, its values are the properties it binds (`v-model` for the value, `disabled`), and its interaction states map to the variants for `data-state`, `:hover`, `:active`, `:focus-visible`, and `[data-disabled]`. Do not reimplement the control's keyboard and accessibility handling. ### Step 3 — Extract tokens ``` list_variables → all variables with values per mode list_collections → collection structure and mode names ``` Map design variables to code tokens. The approach depends on the target stack: #### Tailwind projects Do NOT create CSS custom properties for font sizes, font weights, spacing, or border radius — Tailwind has its own system for these. Use Tailwind utility classes directly: - Font sizes → `text-[13px]`, `text-sm`, `text-base`, etc. - Font weights → `font-bold`, `font-medium`, `font-[600]` - Spacing → `gap-3`, `p-4`, `px-5`, `py-[14px]`, or arbitrary `gap-[12px]` - Border radius → `rounded-xl`, `rounded-[14px]`, `rounded-full` Only create CSS custom properties for **semantic colors** — these are the values that would change across themes. Name them to avoid conflicts with Tailwind's built-in variables (do NOT use names like `--font-bold`, `--text-sm`, `--radius-lg`): ```css :root { --movie-bg: #0f0f1a; --movie-surface: #1a1a2e; --movie-accent: #7c3aed; --movie-text: #ffffff; --movie-text-dim: #ffffff80; } ``` Reference in Tailwind classes: `bg-[var(--movie-bg)]`, `text-[var(--movie-text)]` #### CSS Modules / plain CSS projects Create CSS custom properties for all token categories (colors, spacing, typography, radius). Use a project-specific prefix to avoid collisions: ```css :root { --app-color-bg: #0f0f1a; --app-space-sm: 4px; --app-text-sm: 12px; --app-radius-md: 8px; } ``` #### No design variables in the file If the design has no Figma variables, extract implicit tokens from `analyze_colors` and `analyze_typography` output — identify the de facto palette and type scale. For Tailwind projects, only extract semantic colors as CSS custom properties; use Tailwind utilities for everything else. #### Multi-mode collections (light/dark) - Generate token values for each mode - Use CSS custom properties with class-based switching (`.dark { ... }`) ### Step 4 — Generate code For each component, bottom-up (primitives first, then composites, then screens): ``` get_jsx id= → read structure describe id= → understand semantic role export_svg ids=[] → extract vector assets ``` **Rules:** - One component per file - Component name comes from the Figma node name, converted to PascalCase - Props interface reflects the variable content identified in Step 2 - Use design tokens from Step 3 for semantic colors - For Tailwind: use utility classes directly for spacing, font sizes, weights, radius — do NOT wrap them in `var()` indirection - Match measurements exactly: font sizes, spacing, border radii, colors - Use auto-layout data to determine flex direction, gap, padding, alignment - Preserve text direction and container flow direction separately when the design uses RTL. - Absolute positioning only when `layoutPositioning` is `ABSOLUTE` or layout mode is `NONE` - If a node has `clipsContent: true`, use `overflow: hidden` - Text nodes: preserve font family, size, weight, line height, letter spacing, alignment - Images/illustrations: use `export_svg` for vectors, placeholder `` for raster **Interactive states:** Figma designs rarely include hover/active/focus states unless the component has explicit variants for them. Always add sensible interactive feedback to clickable elements: - **Buttons (primary):** `hover:brightness-110 active:brightness-90 transition-all` - **Buttons (secondary/ghost):** `hover:bg-white/[0.12] active:bg-white/[0.06] transition-colors` - **Icon buttons:** `hover:bg-white/[0.15] active:scale-95 transition-all` - **Cards/list items (if clickable):** `hover:bg-white/[0.04] transition-colors` - **Links/text buttons:** `hover:underline` or `hover:opacity-80` - **All interactive elements:** add `cursor-pointer` and `select-none` - **Focus visible:** add `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-2` with accent color for accessibility If the design HAS explicit hover/active variants (COMPONENT_SET with state property), use those exact styles instead of defaults above. ### Step 5 — Verify After generating code, verify against the design: ``` describe id= → re-check structure matches get_jsx id= → compare JSX structure with generated component tree ``` Check: - All text content from the design appears in the code - All colors reference tokens or use correct hex/opacity values - Spacing values match the design - Component hierarchy matches the design's node tree - No nodes were skipped or merged incorrectly List any deviations with rationale. ## Target stack The user specifies the target stack. ## Plan: Bind typography in `design/design_system.fig`

**Current state**
- 254 text nodes, **0 typography bindings**.
- Existing tokens only cover part of the type system: sizes 14/16; weights 400/600; line-heights 20/24; no tracking tokens; no Inter token.
- Actual values used: sizes `12(151) 13(41) 14(17) 16(40) 20(3) 28(2)`; weights `400 500 600`; line-heights `16 20 22 24 28 36` + auto (`null` on 191 nodes); tracking `0 0.5 0.56`; family `Inter` (254).

**Proposed approach**
1. **Add the missing typography scale** to the document's `Base Palette` collection (leaving existing tokens untouched):
   `base.font.size.12/.13/.20/.28`, `base.font.weight.500`,
   `base.font.line-height.16/.18/.20/.22/.24/.28/.36`,
   `base.font.letter-spacing.0/.0_5/.0_56`, `base.font.family.inter = "Inter"`.
2. **Bind with semantic tokens where they exist**:
   - Button text → `button.font.size`, `button.font.weight`, `button.line-height`
   - TextField label → `label.font.size`; field/placeholder/select/date/color/menu item → `input.font.size`
   - Slider value / page body → `font.body.size`, `font.body.weight`
   - Captions, meta, headings → new base size tokens
   - Line-heights → `control.line-height` (24), `button.line-height` (20), else new base line-height tokens
   - Tracking `0.5/0.56` → new base tracking tokens
   - Family → `base.font.family.inter`
3. **Weights caveat**: OpenPencil's `bind_variable` schema does not expose `fontWeight`. I'll attempt `graph.bindVariable(...,'fontWeight',...)`; if unsupported, weights stay unbound and I'll report it.
4. Verify binding counts, sample nodes, export a PNG, and save.

### Colors — Tier 1

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `color.primary` | Primary brand / accent fill |
| `color.secondary` | Secondary brand / accent fill |
| `color.background` | Document / canvas background |
| `color.surface` | Raised surface (cards, panels, popovers) |
| `color.text.primary` | Primary text color |
| `color.text.secondary` | Secondary / muted text color |
| `color.text.onPrimary` | Text placed on a `color.primary` fill |
| `color.border` | Default border / outline color |
| `color.accent` | Accent for controls (focus, selection, toggle fill) |

Tier 2: `color.separator` (hairline dividers), and status colors
`color.success`, `color.warning`, `color.danger`, `color.info`.

### Typography — Tier 1 core

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `font.body.size` | Body text size |
| `font.body.weight` | Body text weight (100–900) |
| `font.body.family` | Body font family (STRING) |

Tier 2: `font.body.lineHeight`, `font.caption.size`,
`font.heading.1.size`–`font.heading.6.size` (with matching `.weight`/`.family`
paths), `font.mono.family`.

The **predefined typographies** (`TEXT_STYLE`: `LargeTitle`…`Caption2`,
spec/MODIFIERS.md §2) are the semantic counterparts of these token paths: the
renderer owns their concrete size/weight (a baked per-renderer HIG scale). An
application that wants full control can instead bind text to a `TEXT_STYLE` of
its own via the `font.<style>.*` token paths above, or set an explicit
`FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT`/`FONT_FAMILY` override on top.

### Spacing — Tier 1

Spacing is a **generative family** (Tailwind-v4 style): one base unit
multiplied by an arbitrary number.

| Token | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `space.base` | The spacing **unit** (F32) — override this to change the whole density |
| `space.<N>` | `space.base` × N, where N is any positive decimal (`space.1`, `space.2`, `space.0.5`, `space.3.75`) — **computed** by the resolver |

Rules:

1. The `space.<N>` family is **generative**, not independently valued: the
   renderer resolves `space.base` and multiplies by the numeric leaf. Individual
   members MUST NOT be overridden via `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` — override `space.base`
   to control the whole scale.
2. The color-scheme layer and parent fallback apply to `space.base`, never to an
   individual `space.<N>` member (`dark.space.2` is not a token; the dark layer
   is `dark.space.base`).
3. A spacing/padding property MAY carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to any
   `space.<N>` path — e.g. a DSL expresses `.padding(space.2)` or `Space(2)`.
   Literal F32 spacing values remain valid and unthemed.

Tier 2: `size.control.xs` / `sm` / `md` / `lg` — standard control heights.

| `control.padding.horizontal` / `control.padding.vertical` | Control inner padding |

### Per-component tokens

Small sets; only where a component's semantics genuinely differ from
`control.*`. All Tier 1 unless noted.

**Buttons** (Tier 1): `button.background`, `button.foreground`, `button.border`,
`button.radius`, `button.padding`, `button.height`, `button.font.size`,
`button.font.weight`, `button.accent`.

> A composite shorthand such as `button.padding` (two-axis) is renderer-owned:
> the scalar token value types cannot encode a multi-part CSS shorthand. Apps
> that need a scalar override should use the shared control padding tokens or
> per-component properties.

**Text fields / editors** (Tier 1): `input.background`, `input.foreground`,
`input.placeholder`, `input.border`, `input.radius`, `input.font.size`.

**Toggle / switch** (Tier 1): `toggle.accent`, `toggle.track.off`,
`toggle.track.on`, `toggle.thumb`.

**Slider** (Tier 1): `slider.accent`, `slider.track`, `slider.thumb`.

**Progress / gauge** (Tier 1): `progress.track`, `progress.fill`,
`gauge.track`, `gauge.fill`.

**Stepper** (Tier 2): `stepper.accent`, `stepper.background`, `stepper.border`,
`stepper.radius`.

**Picker** (Tier 2): `picker.accent`, `picker.background`, `picker.border`,
`picker.radius`.

**Menu** (Tier 2): `menu.background`, `menu.foreground`, `menu.border`,
`menu.radius`.

**Label** (Tier 2): `label.foreground`, `label.font.size`.

---

## Color Schemes (Light / Dark)

Base token paths define the **light** design. A `dark.`-prefixed path defines
the **dark** design for the same token.

The renderer derives the **effective color scheme** from its platform's native
light/dark signal by default. An application MAY override it for the whole host
with `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` (`platform` / `light` / `dark`); the renderer
applies the override until the application restores `platform`. The
platform-derived signal itself is never carried by the protocol.

# pathland-ts-codegen — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 27, 2026

Generates the TypeScript DOM renderer's protocol-derived files from the canonical
Rust sources, so the TS side cannot drift silently.

## Implemented

- **Window metadata constants**: `CMD_SET_WINDOW_METADATA` + `WINDOW_TITLE/DESCRIPTION/LOCALE` are generated from `pathland_core`.
- **Attributed text**: `CMD_SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` is generated from
  `pathland_core::parameter`.

- **`constants.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/constants.ts`): every wire constant is
  bound to its `pathland_core::constants` source (a rename breaks compilation, a
  revalue changes the emitted file); the protocol-semantic enum codes (alignment,
  shape kind, state, …) are enumerated from `spec/` — `ROLE_*` is bound to
  `pathland_core::constants::role` (the semantic-only catalog, dense 0–13) and
  `TEXT_STYLE_*` to `pathland_core::constants::text_style`.
- **`generated/tokens-core.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/generated/tokens-core.ts`):
  the design-token conventions (`tokenToCssVar`, `tokenToForcedDarkCssVar`,
  `isDarkToken`, `isLengthToken`, `resolveTokenCssRef` + length-token tables)
  emitted from `pathland_render_html::token_spec` — the single source the Rust
  renderer and the DOM client share. `src/tokens.ts` imports it. Explicit
  `dark.` references resolve to `--pl-dark-…` and plain refs carry the
  `unset` fallback.
- **`generated/role-spec.ts`** (`lib/typescript/src/generated/role-spec.ts`):
  the semantic `ROLE` → element + typography → heading conventions emitted from
  `pathland_render_html::role_spec` — `ROLE_TAGS`, `HEADING_STYLES`,
  `ShellKind`, and the `semanticTag`/`textTag`/`ariaRole`/`headingLevel`
  resolvers — so semantic-tag / ARIA / heading decisions cannot drift between
  the Rust SSR renderer and the DOM client. `constants.ts` also carries the
  media surface (`COMPONENT_MEDIA_CONTROLLER`/`VIDEO`, `PROP_MEDIA_SOURCE`/
  `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`/`MEDIA_MUTED`/`MEDIA_LOOP`/`MEDIA_RATE`, and the
  `MEDIA_*` event commands) and the icon surface (`COMPONENT_ICON`,
  `PROP_ICON_NAME`).
- **Icon glyph map — intentionally NOT generated.** The full canonical icon
  catalog (`generated/icons.ts`, ~13KB in the bundle) was **removed**: the DOM
  client no longer carries glyph data. SSR inlines only the icons the page uses,
  and a runtime swap to a name the page did not embed lazily fetches

content.text: The design in openpencil must be the source of truth gping forward. Thats why every single variable must be there. The worflow later on will be that they will be maintained in openpencil and then exported to style dictioarny

Understood — OpenPencil becomes the canonical token source; Style Dictionary is downstream. That changes the plan: **do not edit `design/tokens` or regenerate CSS/fixtures now.** All missing tokens should be authored in the `.fig`, and the future export becomes OpenPencil → DTCG → Style Dictionary.

## Plan: complete typography as OpenPencil source of truth

**1. Complete the variable library in OpenPencil (additive, existing bindings preserved)**
- **Base palette** (new primitives, literals):
  - `base.font.size.12/.13/.20/.28` (14/16 exist)
  - `base.font.weight.500` (400/600 exist)
  - `base.font.line-height.16/.18/.20/.22/.24/.28/.36`
  - `base.font.letter-spacing.0/.0_5/.0_56`
  - `base.font.family.inter = "Inter"` (document stand-in for the system stack)
- **Semantic Tier-2** (aliases/literals):
  - `font.body.lineHeight` (24)
  - `font.caption.size` (12), `font.caption.lineHeight` (16), `font.caption.weight` (400)
  - `font.meta.size` (13), `font.meta.lineHeight` (20), `font.meta.weight` (500)
  - `font.heading.1.size/weight/lineHeight` (28/600/36) and `.family`
  - `font.heading.2.size/weight/lineHeight` (20/600/28) and `.family`
- Keep `Pathland Tokens` and `Base Palette`; create only the new variables so the 533 spacing and color bindings already on nodes survive.

**2. Bind all 254 text nodes**
- `fontSize` → semantic (`font.heading.*`, `font.caption.*`, `font.meta.*`, `font.body.size`, `button.font.size`, `input.font.size`, `label.font.size`, `control.font.size`) else base.
- `lineHeight` → `button.line-height` (20), `control.line-height` (24), new semantic line-heights, else base. Set explicit values for auto text (`12→18`, `13→20`, `14→20`, `16→24`) first, then bind.
- `letterSpacing` → base tracking tokens (`0`, `0.5`, `0.56`).
- `fontFamily` → `base.font.family.inter` for all text.
- `fontWeight`: OpenPencil's `bind_variable` schema does **not** expose `fontWeight`. I'll attempt `graph.bindVariable(...,'fontWeight',...)`; if rejected, weights stay unbound despite the variables existing. I'll report the exact result.

**3. Verify & save**
- Count bound fields per property; confirm 0 unbound typography where a variable exists; export all three pages for visual regression; save `design/design_system.fig`.

## Source-of-truth concerns to resolve

The current file is **not yet exporter-ready**:
- `Pathland Tokens` mixes semantic (64) and component (91) tokens; SD expects separate `base/semantic/component` layers.
- Imported variables currently hold resolved literals, not base↔semantic aliases, so a DTCG export would lose the reference graph.
- DTCG export emits nested token objects and one file per mode; `design/tokens` uses flat dotted keys and `$extensions.pathland.dark`, so a post-export converter will be required later.

Two decisions before I execute:

content.text:
## Plan: OpenPencil as the source of truth

**No repo source changes** — `design/tokens`, `base.css`, CSS hashes, and golden fixtures stay untouched. All work lands in `design/design_system.fig`.

### Phase 0 — Preflight (read-only snapshots)
- Snapshot all 241 variables (name, type, per-mode values, description) and every node binding (`fills/0/color`, `strokes/0/color`, padding, spacing, radius, stroke, type fields, opacity, width/height).
- Export current pages to PNG for visual diffing.
- Reconstruct the layer/reference graph from `design/tokens/**` (base → semantic → component, plus dark targets).
- Probe two capabilities in a throwaway collection, then remove it:
  - **Variable aliases** (`{type: VARIABLE_ALIAS}`) — needed so semantic/component variables reference base and export as SD references.
  - **Per-node variable modes** (`node.variableModes`) — needed to drive Dark variants from the same variables.

### Phase 1 — Restructure collections (export-ready)
- Replace the current two collections with:
  - `Base` — one mode `Value`
  - `Semantic` — `Light` / `Dark`
  - `Component` — `Light` / `Dark`
- Recreate all 241 variables in the right layer with identical names, types, values, and descriptions.
- If aliases are supported: semantic/component values alias base/semantic targets, using the source reference graph (including per-mode dark references). Otherwise store literals and embed the source reference in `description` (e.g. `ref base.color.blue.600`) for the future exporter.
- Add the missing typography variables:
  - Base: sizes `12/13/20/28`, weight `500`, line-heights `16/18/20/22/24/28/36`, tracking `0/0.5/0.56`, `base.font.family.inter`.
  - Semantic: `font.body.lineHeight`, `font.caption.{size,weight,lineHeight}`, `font.meta.{size,weight,lineHeight}`, `font.heading.1.{size,weight,lineHeight,family}`, `font.heading.2.{size,weight,lineHeight,family}`.
- Add audit tokens where values have no token: `toggle.checkbox.radius` (3), `color.swatch.radius` (4), `base.radius.2xl` (16) if the specimen stays.
- Rebind every existing node binding by variable name, verify zero stale IDs, then delete the old collections.

### Phase 2 — Typography binding
- Bind all 254 text nodes: size, line-height, tracking, family; semantic tokens first, base otherwise.
- Set explicit line-heights for auto text (`12→18`, `13→20`, `14→20`, `16→24`) then bind.
- Attempt `fontWeight` binding via `graph.bindVariable`; report if unsupported by the current API.

### Phase 3 — Full tokenization audit
Bind all tokenizable properties, scoped by component/semantic meaning:
- Colors (light already; dark via mode-driven variants if supported)
- Radii (2/6/8/12/9999 plus new 3/4/16 tokens)
- Border widths (`1/2/3`; skip per-stroke focus-ring arrays if per-index binding is unsupported)
- Control/component dimensions: `control.height`, `toggle.*`, `slider.*`, `progress.*`, `gauge.*`, `spinner.*`, `stepper.*`, `menu.min-width`
- Disabled opacity `0.5`
- Leave unbound with rationale: artboard/specimen/demo geometry (page widths, field widths, media 384×216), multi-stroke ring weights, and drop shadows (no bindable effect fields in the API).

### Phase 4 — Verify & save
- Binding counts per family, plus an explicit list of remaining literals and why.
- Export all three pages and visual-diff against the Phase 0 snapshots.
- Run `openpencil tokens … --format dtcg` to a temp folder to validate the future export: verify `$extensions.dev.openpencil.name`, Light/Dark modifiers, aliases, and dimension encoding.
- Save `design/design_system.fig`.

### Phase 5 — Future export path (documented, not built now)
The DTCG output maps cleanly to a converter:
`Base` set + `Semantic`/`Component` modifiers → `design/tokens/{base,semantic,component}/*.tokens.json`, using `$extensions.dev.openpencil.name` for flat dotted keys, Light as `$value`, Dark as `$extensions.pathland.dark`.

Two audit boundaries to confirm:

options.description: Set each Dark component/frame to the Dark variable mode and bind its colors to the same variables. Dark visuals become variable-driven; falls back to explicit literals only if per-node modes are unsupported.
options.label: Mode-driven (Recommended)

options.description: Keep dark variants as explicit dark-value frames. Variables still carry Dark mode values, but dark frames are not bound to them.

questions.question: Should dark variants be driven by variable modes?

options.description: Bind tokenizable design properties (color, type, spacing, radius, border, component sizes, opacity) and leave artboard/demo geometry, multi-stroke rings, and shadows unbound with a documented rationale.
options.label: Token families only (Recommended)

options.description: Also invent tokens for every remaining numeric literal used in the file (specimen sizes, demo widths, swatch dimensions, icon 24, etc.).
options.label: Every literal tokenized

Done. `design/design_system.fig` is now the canonical token source.

**Structure**
- **Base** `Value` — 105 variables
- **Semantic** `Light`/`Dark` — 79 variables
- **Component** `Light`/`Dark` — 93 variables
- Total **277** = all 241 original Style Dictionary variables + 36 new type/radius/component tokens.

**Bindings**
- 3,032 bound fields total.
- **254/254** text nodes bound for `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `fontFamily`.
- **0** unbound radii, stroke weights, opacity, or spacing.
- Dark variants, panels, boards, and instances are set to **Dark variable mode**; opaque dark values are variable-bound.
- `fontWeight` remains unbound (254): OpenPencil rejects it as a bindable field (`Unknown binding field "fontWeight"`); the variables exist and export.

**Export-readiness**
- Verified DTCG export: `Base` set + `Semantic`/`Component` modifiers, each with Light/Dark.
- Original dotted token paths are preserved in `$extensions.dev.openpencil.name`.
- Added export type hints in descriptions for `number`, `duration`, and `fontFamily` tokens (DTCG otherwise defaults FLOATs to dimensions).
- References are stored as literals plus `value ref` / `dark ref` metadata because OpenPencil does not resolve variable aliases for paints.

**Documented exceptions**
- ~66 translucent dark paint fields keep explicit opaque composites; the renderer composites alpha over white, not the parent surface. The Dark variables still carry the true alpha values for export.
- 56 specimen hairline strokes and 1 showcase backdrop are intentionally unbound document decoration, not design tokens.

The file opens on **Foundations**, and its subtitles now state the OpenPencil → Style Dictionary workflow. Note: the unrelated modified `TrackRowView.kt` was not touched by this work.

1: # Pathland base design
2: 
3: The built-in look of the HTML renderer, generated from a **three-layer Style
4: Dictionary pipeline** plus hand-authored reset/component CSS.
5: 
6: ```
7: tokens/base/*.tokens.json        internal palette + scales          (not emitted)
8: tokens/semantic/*.tokens.json    protocol catalog semantics        (emitted)
9: tokens/component/*.tokens.json   per-component surface             (emitted)
10: html/reset.css                   Tailwind-derived preflight        (hand-authored)
11: html/components.css              .pathland-* rules                 (hand-authored)
12: ```
13: 
14: The generated bundle is `build/base.css` (reset + `tokens.css` + components);
15: `build/base.css.name` is its content-hashed asset name (e.g.
16: `base-5f86423db422.css`). Both are synced into
17: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/` and committed: the renderer embeds
18: the bytes with `include_str!` and exposes the name for cache-busting links. There
19: is one built-in base design and no app-facing design selection.
20: 
21: ## Commands
22: 
23: ```sh
24: npm --prefix design ci          # install (CI / clean checkout)
25: npm --prefix design run build   # Style Dictionary + build/base.css
26: npm --prefix design run check   # catalog/layer/dark/dimension validation
27: npm --prefix design run dev     # rebuild on token/CSS changes
28: npm --prefix design run dev -- --serve   # also serve preview/ on :4173
29: scripts/sync-design-css.sh      # copy base.css + base.css.name into the Rust crate
30: scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check
31: ```
32: 
33: After changing tokens or CSS: `npm --prefix design run build`, then
34: `scripts/sync-design-css.sh`, then run `cargo test -p pathland-render-html`.
35: 
36: `build/` and `node_modules/` are gitignored. `package-lock.json` is committed.
37: 
38: ## Tokens
39: 
40: Each token is a flat DTCG entry: `$value`, `$type`, optional `$description` and
41: `$extensions.pathland`. Keys carry their full dotted path because the catalog
42: contains paths that are both a leaf and a group (`control.border` is a color,
43: `control.border.width` is a dimension), which nested DTCG trees cannot represent.
44: 
45: - **base** tokens are literals. They are internal: the generator resolves them
46:   to literals and **never emits them** as CSS variables. Override the semantic
47:   or component token instead.
48: - **semantic** tokens reference base tokens. They are the protocol catalog
49:   surface (`spec/TOKENS.md`).
50: - **component** tokens reference semantic tokens, or a base scale token
51:   (`base.space.*`, `base.radius.*`, `base.border.width.*`, `base.size.*`,
52:   `base.font.*`) when no semantic alias exists. A component token that must
53:   reference a base **color** needs an explicit justification:
54: 
55:   ```json
56:   "$extensions": {
57:     "pathland": { "baseReference": "why this base color is used directly" }
58:   }
59:   ```
60: 
61: ### Dark values
62: 
63: Dark values live on `$extensions.pathland.dark`:
64: 
65: ```json
66: {
67:   "color.primary": {
68:     "$value": "{base.color.blue.600}",
69:     "$type": "color",
70:     "$extensions": { "pathland": { "dark": "{base.color.blue.400}" } }
71:   }
72: }
73: ```
74: 
75: The generator emits four token layers:
76: 
77: 1. `:root` (light),
78: 2. `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not([data-pathland-scheme])`,
79: 3. `:root[data-pathland-scheme='dark']` (forced dark) and
80:    `:root[data-pathland-scheme='light']` (forced light),
81: 4. the forced-dark variable family `--pl-dark-*` for explicit `dark.` token
82:    references.
83: 
84: A reference to another **emitted** token compiles to `var(--pl-<target>)` (and
85: `var(--pl-dark-<target>)` in the forced-dark family), so the target's dark layer
86: wins. A reference to a **base** token compiles to its literal. With no explicit
87: dark value, the dark layers reference the same target variable.
88: 
89: ### Internal tokens
90: 
91: Durations, z-index, and `em` icon sizes are renderer-internal (not part of
92: `spec/TOKENS.md`). Mark them with `$extensions.pathland.internal: true`; they are
93: still emitted and listed in `build/manifest.json` with `"internal": true`.
94: 
95: ## Validation
96: 
97: `npm run check` enforces:
98: 
99: - every Tier-1 token in `pathland_core::TIER1_TOKENS` is present;
100: - layer direction (semantic → base, component → semantic/base scale) and
101:   no unresolved references;
102: - every emitted token has light, platform-dark, forced-dark-scheme, and
103:   forced-dark variable declarations;
104: - every `$type: dimension` token is recognized by the canonical
105:   `isLengthToken` rules in `pathland-render-html::token_spec` (add a rule there
106:   when introducing a new dimension path);
107: - durations / z-index / icon sizes are marked internal;
108: - `build/manifest.json` and `build/tokens.css` match the current sources, and
109:   base tokens are not emitted;
110: - `build/base.css.name` matches the SHA-256 of `build/base.css`.
111: 
112: ## Serving the stylesheet
113: 
114: The renderer supports two deliveries:
115: 
116: - **inline** (the library default, `render_document` / `render`): the whole
117:   base design is a `<style>` block in the document head;
118: - **linked** (`render_document_linked` / Java `renderLinked`): an external
119:   `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{base}/base-<hash>.css">`. Token overrides
120:   (`<style data-pathland-tokens>`) and fit-band rules stay inline after it.
121: 
122: The Spring Boot and Quarkus SSR starters use the linked form and serve the
123: renderer-owned bytes at `{base}/base-<hash>.css` (global and per-app bases) with
124: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. A new design build gets a
125: new hash, so the URL busts the cache. Library hosts can keep the inline default
126: or serve `baseCss()` / `baseCssName()` themselves.
127: 
128: ## Preview
129: 
130: `preview/index.html` loads `build/base.css` and renders representative
131: `.pathland-*` markup (buttons, fields, toggles, slider, progress, stepper, menu,
132: media) with a light/dark/system switcher. Run `npm run dev -- --serve` and open
133: <http://127.0.0.1:4173/>. This is a development tool, not an app-selectable base
134: design.
135: 
136: ## Generated files — do not edit
137: 
138: - `build/tokens.css`
139: - `build/manifest.json`
140: - `build/base.css`
141: - `build/base.css.name`
142: - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css` (synced copy)
143: - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/base.css.name` (synced copy)
144: 
145: Edit the token files or `html/{reset,components}.css`, then rebuild and sync.

(End of file - total 145 lines)
</content>

## Canonical source: OpenPencil

`design_system.fig` is the source of truth for the design system and its
tokens. It contains three variable collections:

| Collection | Modes | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Base` | `Value` | internal palette, type/space/radius scales |
| `Semantic` | `Light` / `Dark` | protocol catalog semantics |
| `Component` | `Light` / `Dark` | per-component token surface |

It currently holds **277 variables**: the 241 variables that mirror
`design/tokens` plus 36 extended tokens needed for full typography and
component coverage (caption/meta/heading sizes, weights, line-heights,
tracking, an Inter family token, extra radius steps, and
`toggle.checkbox.radius` / `color.swatch.radius`). Those 36 are not yet in
`design/tokens` — the next export/transform brings them across.

The three pages are **Foundations** (color/type/spacing/radius specimens),
**Components** (Light/Dark variant sets), and **Showcase** (the preview
reproduced in both themes).

Binding coverage and known limits:

- All 254 text nodes bind `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, and
  `fontFamily`; spacing, radii, border widths, control/component sizes, and
  disabled opacity are bound too.
- `fontWeight` cannot be bound: OpenPencil's `bind_variable` API rejects
  `fontWeight`. The weight variables exist and export.
- Dark components/panels/boards use the **Dark variable mode**. Translucent
  dark surface/border tokens keep explicit opaque composites where the
  renderer would otherwise composite alpha over white instead of the parent
  surface; the Dark variable values remain the true alpha tokens for export.
- Swatch hairline strokes and the showcase page backdrop are intentionally
  unbound document decoration, not design tokens.

### Exporting to Style Dictionary

```sh
openpencil tokens design/design_system.fig --format dtcg --out <dir>
```

This writes a DTCG bundle:

```
Base/Value.tokens.json
Semantic/{Light,Dark}.tokens.json
Component/{Light,Dark}.tokens.json
tokens.resolver.json
```

- The original dotted token path is preserved on every token under
  `$extensions.dev.openpencil.name`.
- Light/Dark values are separate mode files. A transform is still required to
  reproduce this repository's flat `tokens/` format: flatten the dotted key,
  merge the Dark file into `$extensions.pathland.dark`, and map FLOAT types
  using the `dtcg type number|duration|fontFamily` hints in the descriptions.
- References are emitted as literal values (OpenPencil does not resolve variable
  aliases for paints). Each description records the source `value ref` /
  `dark ref`, which the transform uses to restore SD references.

The transform is not wired into CI yet; until it lands, edit the `.fig` in
OpenPencil and update `design/tokens` from the export manually.

```sh
# canonical design source

# downstream Style Dictionary / HTML base design

npm --prefix design run build   # Style Dictionary + build/base.css
npm --prefix design run check   # catalog/layer/dark/dimension validation
npm --prefix design run dev     # rebuild on token/CSS changes
npm --prefix design run dev -- --serve   # also serve preview/ on :4173
scripts/sync-design-css.sh      # copy base.css + base.css.name into the Rust crate
scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check
```

After exporting tokens or changing CSS: `npm --prefix design run build`, then
`scripts/sync-design-css.sh`, then run `cargo test -p pathland-render-html`.
